# package device

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/device"
```

Package device implements a PROFINET IO-Device (conformance class A, RT\_CLASS\_1/2): the DCP responder, the RPC server for Connect, Read, Write, Control and Release, application relationships with their explicit state machine, cyclic input production and output consumption, alarms, diagnosis and identification and maintenance records.

The application describes the device with a [model.Device](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/model#Device), provides input data with [Device.SetInput](#func-device-setinput), reads output data with [Device.Output](#func-device-output) and answers its own records through a [Handler](#type-handler). Process data and protocol processing are kept apart: the device copies data into and out of the cyclic frames on its own goroutines.

## Constants

```go
const AlarmAckTimeout = 5 * time.Second
```

AlarmAckTimeout is the shortest time the device waits for the controller's AlarmAck after the transport acknowledged the alarm.

```go
const DefaultStoreKey = "device"
```

DefaultStoreKey is the key of a device's state in its Config.Store.

### func RecordError

```go
func RecordError(code1, code2 uint8) error
```

RecordError returns the error a Handler returns to answer a Read or Write with an ErrorDecode PNIORW status: code1 is one of the pnio.RW\* values, code2 is application specific. The device fills in the ErrorCode of the service.

### type ARState

```go

```

ARState is the state of an application relationship on the device.

```go
const (
	ARStateNone ARState = iota
	ARStateParameterizing
	ARStateAppReadyPending
	ARStateData
	ARStateClosed
)
```

AR states. An IOCAR goes Parameterizing → AppReadyPending → Data; a PrmBegin returns it from Data to Parameterizing; an IOSAR (device access) is in Data from its Connect. Every state can go to Closed.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Model describes the device; required.
	Model *model.Device
	// Mux is the Layer 2 port; required. With a Bridge it is the mux of
	// the bridge's CPU port (the device's interface).
	Mux *l2.Mux
	// Bridge makes the device a multiport device: each bridge port is a
	// device port (port submodules 0x8001, 0x8002, ... of the model's
	// DAP, which must declare them), with its own MAC address, LLDP agent
	// and link state. nil: the device has one port, Mux's. The caller
	// owns the bridge and closes it after the device.
	Bridge *bridge.Bridge
	// MRP runs media redundancy on two ports of a multiport device (a
	// Bridge is required); nil: none, and the MRP records are refused.
	MRP *MRPConfig
	// SystemRedundancy accepts the IOCARSRs of S2 AR sets: EXPERIMENTAL,
	// not interoperable (sr.go). nil refuses IOCARSR, as before.
	SystemRedundancy *SRConfig
	// StationName and IP are the initial station name and IP suite.
	StationName string
	IP          dcp.IPSuite
	// ListenPacket opens the RPC sockets. nil uses the operating system's
	// UDP stack.
	ListenPacket ListenPacketFunc
	// ApplyIP applies a DCP Set of the IP suite to the IP stack the RPC
	// sockets use. nil only records the new suite (and reports it in
	// DCP); an application on a real interface configures the operating
	// system itself (Handler.IPChanged is called either way).
	ApplyIP func(s dcp.IPSuite, permanent bool) error
	// RPCPort is the port of the RPC server. Zero means 34964.
	RPCPort int
	// ControllerRPCPort is the controller's port that ApplicationReady is
	// sent to when the Connect request has no ARRPCBlockReq. Zero means
	// 34964.
	ControllerRPCPort int
	// Handler receives the events and records the device does not handle
	// itself. nil uses NopHandler.
	Handler Handler
	// IM holds the initial I&M1 to I&M4 records.
	IM IMData
	// RejectSupervisorAR refuses IOSAR (device access) connections.
	RejectSupervisorAR bool
	// DisableLLDP stops the device from sending LLDP.
	DisableLLDP bool
	// LLDPInterval is the LLDP transmit interval. Zero means 5 s.
	LLDPInterval time.Duration
	// NoResponseDelay answers DCP Identify at once (for tests).
	NoResponseDelay bool
	// Hello makes the device announce itself with DCP Hello requests, so
	// that its IO controller can connect without an Identify: a sequence
	// at start and, with a port that reports its link state
	// (l2.LinkStater), whenever the link comes up, while no IO controller
	// is connected. A DCP Set and a Connect end the sequence. The device's
	// DeviceInitiative then reports Hello. Zero (dcp.HelloOff) sends none.
	Hello dcp.HelloMode
	// HelloOptions configure each sequence: the number of Hellos and
	// their interval, and the delay after the link came up in mode
	// dcp.HelloOnLinkUpDelayed. Zero values are the defaults of
	// dcp.HelloOptions.
	HelloOptions dcp.HelloOptions
	// DHCP are the DHCP options (DCP option 3) the device reports in
	// Identify and Get responses, for example dcp.DHCPClientIDFromMAC()
	// and dcp.DHCPControlParameter(dcp.DHCPControlOn). The library has no
	// DHCP client: addressing stays with the operating system, and the
	// device only reports what the application configures.
	DHCP []dcp.DHCPParameter
	// IPFromDHCP reports the initial IP suite as set by DHCP (IP
	// BlockInfo 0x0002) until a DCP Set changes it.
	IPFromDHCP bool
	// SetDHCP receives a DCP Set of a DHCP option; when it returns
	// dcp.BlockErrorNone the device reports the new value. nil refuses
	// every such Set with "option not supported".
	SetDHCP func(p dcp.DHCPParameter, permanent bool) dcp.BlockError
	// DCPPolicy restricts the DCP responder: a read-only mode (Set
	// refused, Identify and Get answered), rate limits per source for
	// Identify responses and Set requests, and audit events for every Set,
	// ResetToFactory and refused request. The zero value restricts nothing.
	DCPPolicy dcp.Policy
	// ApplicationReadyTimeout bounds the ApplicationReady call. Zero
	// means 6 s (p-net's 3 tries of 2 s).
	ApplicationReadyTimeout time.Duration
	// Store keeps what the device must remember across a restart: the
	// station name and IP suite of a permanent DCP Set, DHCP options and
	// the I&M records (persist.go says what and when). At start its values
	// replace StationName, IP, DHCP and IM. nil keeps everything in
	// memory, as before.
	Store store.Store
	// StoreKey is the device's key in Store; empty means
	// DefaultStoreKey. Devices that share a Store need their own keys.
	StoreKey string
	// SNMP starts a read-only SNMPv1/v2c agent on UDP port 161 (opened
	// with ListenPacket) with MIB-II and the LLDP-MIB. nil, the
	// default, runs none.
	SNMP *SNMPConfig
	// Logger receives diagnostics. nil logs nothing.
	Logger profinet.Logger
	// Metrics receives the AR state changes, connects, aborts, record
	// requests and alarms of the device. nil collects nothing.
	Metrics profinet.Metrics
}
```

Config configures a [Device](#type-device).

### type Device

```go
type Device struct {

	// mrpMu serializes MRP entity replacement and its stop.

	// snmpStart is when the SNMP agent started (sysUpTime 0).

	// The persistent state (persist.go): storeMu serializes the saves,
	// stored is what the store holds (savedRaw its encoding, when this
	// device saved or loaded it), storeErr why it was not used.

	// mu guards the station state and the ARs.

	// reserved counts the Connects in progress, reservedIO those of
	// IOCARs; arSeq numbers the Connects.

	// replacing are the ARs Connects in progress replace (reruns).

	// connecting are the ARUUIDs of the Connects in progress: a second
	// Connect for one of them is refused until the first ends.

	// resetting is set while a DCP ResetToFactory runs: Connects are
	// refused.

	// pdPoke wakes the PDev check evaluator.

	// dhcp are the DHCP options DCP reports; ipDHCP marks ip as set by
	// DHCP. Both under mu.

	// imgMu guards the process data images; it is never held while
	// another lock is taken.

	// owner is the IOCAR that owns each submodule and claimers the IOCARs
	// that may (shared device, owner.go).

	// srSets are the AR sets of system redundancy, guarded by mu.

	// rpcPort is cfg.RPCPort, validated by New.

	// wg tracks the device's goroutines; Close waits for them. A
	// goroutine started after Close began (d.closed) would race with
	// Wait, so goAbort checks closed under mu.

}
```

Device is a PROFINET IO-Device. Its methods are safe for concurrent use.

#### func (Device) AddDiagnosis

```go
func (d *Device) AddDiagnosis(ctx context.Context, slot, subslot uint16, item pnio.DiagnosisItem) error
```

AddDiagnosis records a diagnosis of a submodule and reports it to the controllers with a diagnosis alarm. The item's ChannelProperties specifier is set to "appears". The diagnosis is recorded even when no AR can receive the alarm (it is then reported as an error matching profinet.ErrInvalidState).

#### func (Device) SendAlarm

```go
func (d *Device) SendAlarm(ctx context.Context, al Alarm) error
```

SendAlarm sends an alarm to the controller of every AR in the Data state that owns the submodule, and waits for each acknowledgement. It returns an error matching profinet.ErrNotFound for an unknown submodule, profinet.ErrInvalidState when no AR can receive it, profinet.ErrTimeout when an acknowledgement did not arrive and a \*pnio.StatusError when the controller acknowledged with an error.

SetInput sets the input data and provider status of a submodule; the next cyclic frame of every AR carries it. data must have the submodule's input length.

### type Handler

```go
type Handler interface {
	// ReadRecord reads a record the device does not serve itself: user
	// indices (0..0x7FFF) without a model.Record, and indices the device
	// does not know. Return a *pnio.StatusError (see RecordError) to
	// answer with a PNIO status.
	ReadRecord(ctx context.Context, r RecordRequest) ([]byte, error)

	// WriteRecord writes such a record. Writes of model.Records are
	// validated and stored by the device and then reported here; an error
	// rejects the write.
	WriteRecord(ctx context.Context, r RecordRequest, data []byte) error

	// PrmEnd reports the end of parameterization of an AR. When it
	// returns nil the device sends ApplicationReady; an error aborts the
	// AR. It may block until the application is ready (within the CM
	// activity timeout of the AR).
	PrmEnd(ctx context.Context, ar ARInfo) error

	// StateChanged reports every state transition of an AR, one at a time
	// and in the order the AR went through them. It may be called from a
	// different goroutine than the one that caused the transition, and
	// after that goroutine went on.
	StateChanged(ar ARInfo, from, to ARState)

	// AlarmAck reports the acknowledgement of an alarm by the controller.
	AlarmAck(ar ARInfo, ack pnio.AlarmAck)

	// Signal is a DCP request to flash the signal LED.
	Signal()

	// ResetToFactory is a DCP request to reset; mode is one of the
	// dcp.Reset* values. The device then aborts its ARs and resets what
	// the mode covers. Return an error code to refuse.
	ResetToFactory(mode uint16) dcp.BlockError

	// NameChanged and IPChanged report a DCP Set.
	NameChanged(name string, permanent bool)
	IPChanged(s dcp.IPSuite, permanent bool)
}
```

Handler receives what the device leaves to the application. Every method is called on a device goroutine and should return promptly. Embed [NopHandler](#type-nophandler) to implement only some of them.

### type SNMPConfig

```go
type SNMPConfig struct {
	// Community is the read community; required.
	Community string
	// Contact and Location are sysContact and sysLocation.
	Contact, Location string
	// Description is sysDescr; empty uses the model's TypeOfStation (what
	// LLDP sends as the system description).
	Description string
	// ObjectID is sysObjectID; nil serves zeroDotZero.
	ObjectID snmp.OID
	// Port is the agent's UDP port; zero means 161.
	Port int
	// Rate limits the requests per second (snmp.Config.Rate); zero
	// means snmp.DefaultRate, negative no limit.
	Rate float64
}
```

SNMPConfig turns on the device's read-only SNMPv1/v2c agent (package snmp): the system, interfaces and snmp groups of MIB-II and the LLDP-MIB, the network management objects that PI's conformance class B asks for. The community string travels in clear text and is the only access control.
